biography: Peter Van Delm's journey began on the rain-slicked karting tracks of Genk, Belgium. His father, a mechanic with a local touring car team, instilled a love for speed and precision early on. Young Peter showed flashes of brilliance, but his inconsistency often held him back. A defining moment came at the 2012 Belgian Karting Championship, where, after leading comfortably, he spun out on the last corner, costing him the title. This heartbreak fueled a move to single-seaters, where he showed promise in Formula Renault, even scoring a podium at Spa-Francorchamps. However, he never quite reached the heights predicted, bouncing between various GT series. Now, at 36, Van Delm finds himself in the Ultima GTR series, battling younger talents and struggling to recapture his earlier form. Whispers of retirement grow louder with each passing season, but the stubborn Belgian clings to the hope of one last glorious victory, one last reminder of the potential that once burned so bright. His recent performance at Zolder was particularly disheartening, a collision with a barrier during qualifying relegating him to the back of the grid, a far cry from his ambition to challenge for the lead.
drivingStyle: Van Delm's driving style is a curious mix of aggression and hesitation. When confident, he attacks corners with a late-braking, oversteer-inducing approach, often maximizing entry speed. However, under pressure, his style becomes erratic, prone to locking up brakes and missing apexes. Tire management has always been a weakness, as he tends to overheat the front tires early in a stint due to his aggressive cornering. He is known to be a strong qualifier, often extracting the maximum from the car in short bursts, but struggles to maintain consistency over longer race distances.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision at the 2018 Spa 24 Hours. Van Delm accused Dubois of deliberately squeezing him into the wall, costing him a potential podium finish.
A fierce on-track battle for position in the 2021 GT Challenge Europe series. Rostova consistently outpaced Van Delm, leading to frustration and several heated exchanges in the paddock.
Both racing for limited sponsorships, they constantly compete for the same opportunities, creating a tense atmosphere off the track and aggressive maneuvers on it.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Must eat a specific brand of Belgian chocolate bar exactly one hour before the race.
Refuses to drive a car with a number ending in '3'.
nickname: The Belgian Waffle (because he's either perfectly crisp or a soggy mess, no in-between)
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being the fastest, it's about being the least slow."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2015 Blancpain Endurance Series race at Monza after a daring late-race pass on the leading Ferrari.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2017 Nürburgring 24 Hours, costing his team a certain victory.
